# LiFePO4 vs. NMC

**For most people, LiFePO4 (also called LFP) is the better choice.** NMC's only real advantage is lower weight, and in finished power stations that advantage is often small.

## How they compare

| | **LiFePO4 (LFP)** | **NMC** |
|---|---|---|
| **Rated cycle life** | Typically 3,000–6,000 cycles | Typically 500–1,000 cycles |
| **Daily use lifespan** | About 8–11 years | About 1.5–2 years at 500 cycles |
| **Safety if a cell fails** | Burns cooler and slower | More violent, with flames |
| **Weight** | Somewhat heavier | Lighter at the cell level |
| **Price** | Now mainstream and often cheaper per Wh | Mostly older or compact models |

**Cycle life:** At one full cycle a day, a 500-cycle NMC unit hits its 80% capacity point in about 1.4 years. A 3,000-cycle LFP unit takes about 8 years. ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/))

**Safety:**
- In lab tests, a failing NMC cell peaked at 731 °C and a failing LFP cell at 259 °C. ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/))
- LFP is not fireproof, and one study found it went into thermal runaway earlier when overcharged. ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/))
- When it did fail, it gave off smoke without flames, which matters for a unit kept indoors or in a vehicle.

**Weight:** NMC cells store much more energy per pound. In a finished station, though, the case, inverter and fans weigh the same either way.
- Across one 54-model database, NMC stations held only about 10% more energy per pound. ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/))
- One LFP model, the Anker SOLIX C1000, holds more energy per pound than the NMC Goal Zero Yeti 1000 Lithium. ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/))

**Price:** One database lists a median of $0.55 per Wh for LiFePO4 and $0.95 for NMC. ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc))

**Cold weather:** This is about even. Most stations of either type won't charge below 32 °F, so check the manual of the model you're considering. ([Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc))

## Which should you pick?

- **Daily or frequent use** (van, RV, off-grid, daily solar charging): LiFePO4, clearly.
- **Indoor home backup:** LiFePO4, for its milder failure behavior.
- **A few outages or trips a year:** Either works, because the battery will age with time before it runs out of cycles. Choose on price and weight, and be skeptical of an old NMC model priced like a new LFP one.
- **You already own a working NMC unit:** Keep using it.

Whichever you choose, make sure the size and inverter output fit what you'll run, such as a fridge's startup surge. That matters more than the chemistry.

## One example product

The **BLUETTI Elite 200 V2** is a 2,073 Wh LiFePO4 station with a 2,600 W inverter and a 6,000-cycle rating. It's listed at $899 and suits home backup for a fridge, router and lights. One limitation is that you can't add batteries to it later.
